Start here

Ways in

You do not have to start at the beginning. Sigma has several doors onto the same chain, depending on how finished your starting point is.

In plain words
  • If all you have is an idea, start with a Dossier: a short, fixed interview that writes the idea down as one ticket.
  • If you already have a clear piece of work, file it as a goal and let the loop pick it up.
  • If the backlog is already full, just start the loop.
  • If you are part-way through, you can run a single phase on its own: plan, implement or review.

The doors

Left: where you are. Right: the stage you join. Joining part-way does not skip the record; see the caution below.

Each door

DoorUse it whenStart withWhat you get
1. Raw ideaYou have a sentence, not a spec/sigma-dossier. For a requirements file of any shape, /sigma-prd-intakeOne ticket of intent, then a design, a confirmation and slices that enter the backlog
2. A goal needing a mapA goal exists but nobody checked what it touches/sigma-goal-design, then /sigma-goal-review. With the design gate on, the loop files this for youA design file, and on confirmation the sdlc:designed label
3. A scoped goalYou know what you want and how you will know it is doneFile an issue labelled sdlc:goal, or a file under .sdlc/goals/. /sigma-brainstorm shapes one; /sigma-scope turns a rough idea into filed, ordered issuesA goal the loop can pick
4. The backlogGoals are queued/sigma-loop unattended, or /sigma-goal for one goal with your approval at each gateEvery goal through all phases, or parked with a reason
5 to 7. Mid-wayYou already hold part of the work/sigma-plan, /sigma-implement or /sigma-reviewThat phase, run on its own
Joining part-way is not skipping

You can run a phase by itself. But a goal is only recorded done when the record shows the earlier phases ran. Research and retro can be waived for a trivial goal, with the waiver recorded; plan, plan-review, implement and review never can. If you start at Implement, plan the work and have the plan reviewed first, or the run cannot finish cleanly.

Technical detail

The idea door

  • Dossier. Eight questions, asked in order, one at a time. Up to three answered follow-ups may be added, and any doubt it cannot settle is recorded as an open question rather than guessed. The ticket is labelled story and is never sdlc:goal, so the loop cannot pick it.
  • Requirements file. Each answer must cite a quote from the file. A gap becomes an open question. A source file from the repository is refused as the input.
  • Design. Writes a design file under .sdlc/design/ and a comment. It creates no ticket and no label.
  • Review. The independent confirmation. Only on confirmation does it add sdlc:designed and create the epic and its slices. A rejection writes one comment.
  • No resume. The Dossier ticket does not exist until it is filed, so an interrupted interview starts over.

The existing-goal door

This is the same design pass reached from a different entrance. No Dossier is involved: the goal is the input. When the design concludes the goal is one coherent unit, no epic is created and the label alone is the output.

The backlog door

The loop picks an open goal with no open prerequisite, runs the pick-time checks, then each phase as its own subagent. The three ways to run (/sigma-goal, /sigma-goal <N> --land, /sigma-loop) are compared in the running guide; see Running unattended.

The mid-way doors

  • Each phase command is a standalone skill. Running it records nothing about the phases before it.
  • The phase-record gate ships on and is checked when a goal is recorded done and when a pull request is merged. It needs the action log enabled, and refuses rather than pass unverified without it.
  • Not measured: how often people join mid-way in practice. The behaviour above is read from the skills and the gate's documented rules, not from usage data.
